microarchitecture_summary.implementation_style: Single-clock synthesizable RTL with one free-running 8-bit PWM carrier counter, one slower rate counter or divider, one 8-bit duty register, and one direction bit.
microarchitecture_summary.control_strategy: On every clk edge, the PWM carrier increments continuously and the LED output is driven by a simple carrier-versus-duty comparison. A slower update event advances the duty register up or down and flips direction at the endpoints so the brightness repeatedly breathes.
microarchitecture_summary.state_strategy: Use only a small set of synchronous registers: an 8-bit PWM counter, a slower internal counter for update timing, an 8-bit duty-cycle register, and a direction bit. Initialize to a benign low- or mid-brightness starting condition consistent with FPGA-friendly initialization behavior.
microarchitecture_summary.output_strategy: Drive led directly from the PWM comparison result so the output is active-high and visibly modulated by the slow duty-cycle ramp.

fsm_intent.description: No explicit FSM is required. The breathing behavior is implemented as simple synchronous counter-based state updates with direction reversal at the duty-cycle bounds.

internal_storage: slow internal counter or divider used to generate periodic duty update timing
1-bit direction flag indicating incrementing or decrementing phase
output_mapping: led is asserted when the PWM carrier value is less than the duty-cycle register, otherwise deasserted.

sequencing_notes: The PWM carrier increments on every rising edge of clk.
The slow counter increments on clk and generates a periodic update event much less frequently than the PWM carrier cycle.
On each update event, the duty-cycle register increments when direction indicates ramp-up and decrements when direction indicates ramp-down.
When the duty-cycle register reaches the minimum or maximum bound, the direction bit reverses so the sequence repeats continuously.
State sequencing remains entirely within the clk domain with no resets or cross-domain signals.
timing_notes: The PWM carrier should run much faster than the visible breathing update rate to avoid perceptible flicker.
The slow counter modulus should be chosen to produce human-visible fade timing on a 50 MHz board clock.
The design is intended to be straightforward for synthesis and timing review, with only simple counters and a comparator in the critical path.
ownership_notes: Top-level port names and filename remain exactly as defined in digital_spec_json.
No additional modules, hidden interfaces, memories, vendor primitives, or testbench-only logic are implied.
Starter board constraints are a separate deliverable and must be generated after board selection using PCF for iCE40 boards or LPF for ECP5 boards.
The RTL intent is meant for FPGA open-source flows such as Yosys and nextpnr and should remain synthesizable and lint-friendly.
consistency_notes: Interfaces remain exactly as defined in digital_spec_json.
